title: Pueblos Blancos: Grazalema, Setenil & the Road Down to Vejer
subRegion: Sierra de Grazalema & the Cádiz–Málaga white villages

bestPeriod.window: Late March–early June & mid September–early November
bestPeriod.avoid: July–August (inland highs of 38–42°C, sierra trails closed for fire risk 1 June–15 October) and late November–January, when Grazalema takes Spain's heaviest rainfall
bestPeriod.raw: Late March–early June & mid September–early November

accommodation.note: Two bases; €70–€120 pp/night in small village hotels

food.note: €10–€16 venta mains, one €45 tasting dinner in Vejer

transport.note: Rental car essential — rural buses run 1–2 times a day

activities.note: Cooking class, cheese dairy, Vía Verde bike hire, park permits

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — steep whitewashed lanes, one optional 12 km greenway ride and short sierra walks; nothing technical

gatewayAirport: XRY — Jerez de la Frontera, 1 h 15 to Grazalema; AGP Málaga is the bigger-choice alternative at 2 h to Grazalema, 1 h 20 to Ronda
summary: Two bases, one long descent. You spend four nights high in Grazalema at 823 m, where the sierra rains hardest and the wool is still woven, then drop three nights to Vejer de la Frontera within sight of the Atlantic. In between are the villages that make the route famous — Zahara on its castle rock, Setenil built under an overhanging cliff, Olvera at the head of a disused railway now turned greenway. The pacing is unhurried by design: one move, two open afternoons, and no day that asks for more than 70 km of driving. It suits people who like a village square at 21:00, cheese bought from the person who made it, and a week where the best hours are the ones with nothing scheduled.

itinerary.title: Up into the sierra
itinerary.morning: Land at Jerez, pick up the car, and take the A-382 then A-372 east through El Bosque. Stop at the Centro de Visitantes El Bosque to pick up park information and, if you plan restricted-zone walking, to sort permits.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive in Grazalema, park below the centre and check in. Walk the village end to end — it takes twenty minutes — and end on Plaza de España with a beer and a plate of chicharrones.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Cádiz El Chico on the square: sierra stews, local lamb, and a wine list that leans Cádiz rather than Rioja.
itinerary.dayStats: XRY–Grazalema 95 km / 1 h 15. Grazalema at 823 m. Village walk 1.4 km. Shops shut 14:00–17:30.

itinerary.title: Wool, cheese and the highest village
itinerary.morning: Artesanía Textil de Grazalema when the looms are running — the mill weaves merino blankets and ponchos the village has made since the 18th century. Buy the plain undyed manta, not the souvenir throw.
itinerary.afternoon: The 12 km run south to Villaluenga del Rosario for Queso Payoyo: taste the semicurado, the sheep's cheese rolled in rosemary, and the manteca-cured wheels. Walk the village's stone bullring, oval and set into the rock, then look into the sinkhole of the Sima de Villaluenga at the edge of town.
itinerary.evening: Back in Grazalema, Mesón El Simancón for tagarninas and payoyo-stuffed pork.
itinerary.dayStats: Grazalema–Villaluenga 12 km / 20 min. Villaluenga at 858 m — highest in Cádiz province. Cheese €12–€22/kg. Mill mornings roughly 09:00–14:00.

itinerary.title: Zahara, a mountain pass, and an empty afternoon
itinerary.morning: Drive the CA-9104 over Puerto de las Palomas to Zahara de la Sierra — the best road in Andalucía, with the reservoir opening below you at the top. Climb to the Nazrid keep for the view down the Zahara–El Gastor lake.
itinerary.afternoon: Nothing. Back over the pass by 14:30, then a book and a terrace. The sierra light between 17:00 and 20:00 does the work for you.
itinerary.evening: Tapas rather than dinner — work along Plaza de España and Calle Agua, ordering one plate per bar.
itinerary.dayStats: Grazalema–Zahara 17 km / 30 min via Puerto de las Palomas, 1,357 m. Castle path 1.2 km / 180 m ascent. Zahara village at 511 m.

itinerary.title: Setenil under the rock, Olvera above the greenway
itinerary.morning: Setenil de las Bodegas, where Calle Cuevas del Sol and Cuevas de la Sombra run under a genuine overhanging cliff — houses with a mountain for a roof. Coffee at a terrace table with 30 metres of rock above it.
itinerary.afternoon: North to Olvera: the church of Nuestra Señora de la Encarnación and the Moorish castle share one small ridge, and La Cilla below explains the Vía Verde. Hire bikes at the old station and ride out towards the Peñón de Zaframagón to watch griffon vultures.
itinerary.evening: Return to Grazalema for the last night; eat at a venta on the way rather than arriving late and hungry.
itinerary.dayStats: Grazalema–Setenil 33 km / 45 min; Setenil–Olvera 16 km / 25 min; Olvera–Grazalema 38 km / 50 min. Vía Verde 36 km total, 30 tunnels; Olvera–Zaframagón 12 km each way, near-flat. Bike hire €12–€18/day.

itinerary.title: Down through Arcos to the Atlantic light
itinerary.morning: Leave the sierra westward via Ubrique, the leather town, where workshops still cut and stitch for luxury houses. Then Arcos de la Frontera: Plaza del Cabildo on its cliff edge, the Basílica de Santa María, and the balcony over the Guadalete.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue south-west to Vejer de la Frontera. Park outside the walls — the old town's lanes are barely car-width — and check in. First walk: the Arco de la Segur, the Judería, and the walls at sunset.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at El Jardín del Califa, in the Moorish garden of the Califa hotel: Moroccan-leaning cooking, tagines, and a courtyard that stays cool.
itinerary.dayStats: Grazalema–Arcos 60 km / 1 h; Arcos–Vejer 65 km / 1 h. Vejer at 190 m, 10 km from the Atlantic. Walls circuit 1.8 km.
itinerary.sleep: La Casa del Califa, Vejer de la Frontera

itinerary.title: Market, cooking class, and an open afternoon
itinerary.morning: Shop the Mercado de Abastos with Annie B's Spanish Kitchen, then cook the haul — retinto beef, Barbate tuna, sherry from El Puerto — through a long, unhurried session with a roof terrace to eat it on.
itinerary.afternoon: Blank on purpose. Sleep it off, or drive 12 km to El Palmar for a flat empty beach and a chiringuito.
itinerary.evening: Late tapas inside the Mercado de Abastos itself, where the old market stalls now serve small plates from about 20:00.
itinerary.dayStats: Cooking class roughly 5–6 h, around €130–€160. Vejer–El Palmar 12 km / 18 min. Market tapas from 20:00, closed Sunday evening.
itinerary.sleep: La Casa del Califa, Vejer de la Frontera

itinerary.title: Last plaza, then out
itinerary.morning: Coffee on Plaza de España with the tiled fountain, then a slow last loop of the walls before the town wakes properly.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive north to Jerez — an hour — with time for a sherry bodega if your flight is late.
itinerary.dayStats: Vejer–XRY 65 km / 1 h; Vejer–AGP 195 km / 2 h 15. Add 45 min for the Jerez return in August.

accommodationStrategy.name: Casa de las Piedras
accommodationStrategy.description: A plain, long-running family hotel a minute off Plaza de España, with a mix of simple older rooms and renovated ones in the annexe. It is not luxurious, and that is why it works: parking nearby, breakfast from 08:00 for early sierra walks, and staff who know exactly which trails are open. Roughly €65–€95 per double.

accommodationStrategy.name: La Casa del Califa
accommodationStrategy.description: A warren of interconnected buildings on Plaza de España with Moorish and 16th-century fabric, a garden restaurant, and rooms reached by staircases you will get lost in for two days. Directly on the plaza, so you can go out for one drink and come back. Roughly €120–€180 per double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Fuerte Grazalema or Casa Rural La Mimbrera
accommodationStrategy.description: If Casa de las Piedras is full, take a rural house on the Grazalema–Benamahoma road instead of dropping to a chain in Ronda; the point of this week is waking inside the park boundary, not near it.

logistics.connectivity: Spain is in the EU roaming zone. 4G is fine in every village named here; the Vía Verde tunnels, Garganta Verde and the Puerto de las Palomas road have dead patches. Download the Cádiz–Málaga area offline.
logistics.emergency: 112 covers everything including mountain rescue and Guardia Civil. Sierra de Grazalema trails have no phone coverage in the gorges — leave a route note at your hotel.
logistics.weather: Grazalema records the highest annual rainfall in Spain, roughly 2,000 mm, concentrated November–March; a wet day here is genuinely wet. Summer inland highs hit 38–42°C while Vejer stays 6–8°C cooler thanks to the Atlantic levante and poniente winds, which blow hard enough on the coast to close beach umbrellas.
logistics.bookingWindows: Restricted-zone park permits (Garganta Verde, El Pinsapar, Llanos del Rabel) must be requested in advance through the Junta de Andalucía's Sierra de Grazalema reservation system — do it 2–4 weeks out for spring weekends. Annie B's classes book weeks ahead in spring and autumn. El Jardín del Califa needs 2–3 days.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are standard in hotels and town restaurants, but ventas, cheese dairies and market stalls often want cash — carry €80–€100. Tipping is light: round up, or 5% on a full dinner.
logistics.transportRules: A car is effectively mandatory. Rural bus links exist — Transportes Generales Comes between Cádiz, Ubrique and Grazalema, and Los Amarillos between Ronda and Zahara/Grazalema — but typically run once or twice a day and not at all on Sundays. Village centres in Vejer, Arcos and Setenil are too narrow to drive; use the outer car parks. Fuel up in Ronda, Olvera or El Bosque, not in the small villages.
logistics.permits: The high-risk fire season (1 June–15 October) closes several sierra routes entirely. Wild camping is prohibited in the natural park. Drones need authorisation over the park and are banned over the villages.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable throughout. The sierra is limestone with sudden drops and no railings on the castle paths; take proper shoes. Sun exposure inland is severe from May — the villages are white for a reason.

proTips: Drive the CA-9104 from Grazalema to Zahara in the late afternoon rather than the morning: the Puerto de las Palomas viewpoint faces so that the reservoir lights up around 18:00, and the coach traffic has gone.
Buy your payoyo at the Villaluenga dairy, not in Grazalema's souvenir shops. Ask for vacuum-packing if you're flying — it doubles the safe carry time.
Setenil is a two-hour town swamped by day-trippers between 11:00 and 16:00. Arrive at 09:30, and eat in Olvera instead.
The Vía Verde is best ridden Olvera-to-Zaframagón and back rather than end-to-end: you get the vulture colony, the tunnels and the viaducts without needing a shuttle from Puerto Serrano.

Learn the sierra eating clock. Ventas serve lunch 13:30–16:00 and often shut afterwards; village restaurants don't take dinner orders before 20:30. Plan a late lunch and a very late dinner, not the reverse.
In Grazalema, ask at your hotel each morning which park zones are open. Permit availability, fire risk and rain all shift the answer daily, and the posted signs lag reality.
Vejer's Mercado de Abastos is a functioning food market by day and a tapas hall at night. Do both — morning for the tuna and the retinto, evening for the small plates.

raw.Plaza de España, Grazalema: is the hinge of the week: the church of Nuestra Señora de la Aurora on one side, three bar terraces on the others, and a fountain that the whole village passes twice a day. Shops shut 14:00–17:30; the square refills from 20:00 and is fullest at 21:30, an hour later than northern Spain.
raw.Plaza de España, Vejer: works to a different clock — Andalusian-tiled, palm-shaded, and busy from 19:30, with the paseo running out through the Arco de la Segur and along the walls.
raw.Artesanía Textil de Grazalema: on the A-372 at the village edge still weaves pure merino blankets on the town's centuries-old looms (the Merino Royale line). Weekday mornings are when you'll see the machines running; call before a Friday afternoon visit.
raw.Queso Payoyo, Villaluenga del Rosario: — the dairy and shop for the goat and sheep cheese named after the payoya goat breed. Villaluenga is the smallest municipality in Cádiz province and sits at 858 m, the highest village in the sierra.
raw.Vía Verde de la Sierra: 36 km of former railbed between Olvera and Puerto Serrano, through 30 tunnels and over four viaducts, passing the Peñón de Zaframagón griffon vulture colony. Bike hire at both end stations; an out-and-back from Olvera to Zaframagón is 12 km each way and almost flat.
raw.Venta culture: roadside ventas are where sierra cooking actually lives — sopa de tomate, chicharrones, venison in season, plates at €8–€14. They open early, close mid-afternoon, and rarely take cards.
raw.Hands-on experience: a day cooking class at **Annie B's Spanish Kitchen** in Vejer — market shopping first, then sherry, tapas and Andalusian technique in a house with a roof terrace over the plain.
raw.Pacing: one town move all week (Grazalema → Vejer on Day 5), full unstructured afternoons on Days 3 and 6, and short village-to-village walks where they exist — Grazalema to Benamahoma on the old Camino (7 km downhill), Zahara's castle path (1.2 km, 180 m).
